title.rendered: You Are the Salt of the Earth: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “You are the salt of the earth.” A morning devotional on the quiet, preserving presence of a Christian in the world.

content.rendered:
Salt is a strange substance. It does its best work when it disappears into what it is added to. Draw too much attention to it, and it becomes inedible. Withdraw it altogether, and everything it was flavoring dies. Jesus said the believer, in a watching world, is meant to be exactly like that.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, September 5, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt loses its flavor, how shall it be seasoned? It is then good for nothing but to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by men.”
Matthew 5:13 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Salt is a strange substance. Pour it out of a jar and it disappears into whatever you sprinkle it on. Rub it into meat and it draws out moisture, slowing decay. Drop it into a pot of soup and the whole pot tastes richer. Add too much and it becomes inedible. Add none and everything it was seasoning goes flat. Salt does its best work when it disappears into what it is added to. In the ancient world, salt was so valuable that Roman soldiers received a salt ration called the salarium, which is where the English word “salary” comes from. To be “worth your salt” meant to earn what you cost. Jesus takes that everyday substance, so ordinary in the kitchen and so precious in the marketplace, and applies it to His disciples.

“You are the salt of the earth.” Jesus is continuing the Sermon on the Mount, moving from the beatitudes (the character of the Kingdom people) to the calling of the Kingdom people. He does not say to His disciples, “Try to become salt.” He says, “You are the salt of the earth.” The believer’s saltiness is not a project to complete. It is an identity already granted, to be walked in with faithfulness.

The Passion Translation captures the calling with striking imagery: “Your lives are like salt among the people. But if you, like salt, become bland, how can your ‘saltiness’ be restored? Flavorless salt is good for nothing and will be thrown out and trampled on by others” (Matthew 5:13 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “You are the salt of the earth; but if salt has lost its taste (its strength, its quality), how can its saltness be restored? It is not good for anything any longer but to be thrown out and trodden underfoot by men” (Matthew 5:13 AMPC).

Salt in the ancient world did several jobs at once. It preserved meat from spoiling. It flavoured food that was otherwise bland. It was rubbed on newborn babies to symbolise purification. It was included in every grain offering in the Temple as a sign of the covenant with God (see Leviticus 2:13). And Paul tells believers in Colossians 4:6 to let their conversation be “always with grace, seasoned with salt.” Salt is preservative, flavouring, purifying, and covenantal all at once. When Jesus calls His disciples salt, He is placing an enormous vocation on them. The believer, in the ordinary rhythms of everyday life, is meant to slow the decay of the world, add flavour to it, model the purity of Christ, and testify to the covenant God has made.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is your identity. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you are the salt of the earth. Not the sugar. Not the water. The salt. The world around you may not always want your saltiness. It may prefer bland. It may prefer decay. It may push back against the way your presence changes the atmosphere in the room. That is exactly what Jesus was talking about. Do not lose your flavour to fit in. The world does not need more salt-that-is-not-salt. It needs believers who are exactly what Jesus said they are. Preservative. Flavouring. Purifying. Covenantal. You are the salt of the earth. Walk in it today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have made me the salt of the earth. This is not a job I earn. It is an identity Jesus placed on me. Today I refuse to lose my flavour to fit in. I walk into every room I enter as one who preserves against decay, adds flavour to blandness, testifies to the purity of Christ, and carries the covenant of God. My presence changes the atmosphere because You are with me. Let me be exactly what Jesus said I am today, faithfully and unashamedly. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am the salt of the earth. My presence preserves, flavours, purifies, and testifies to the covenant of God. I refuse to lose my flavour today. I walk in the vocation Jesus placed on me.
